item.title: Aslaug
item.description:
Aslaug

Aslaug (Old Norse: Áslaug [ˈɑːsˌlɔuɣ]), also known as Aslög, Aslǫg, Kraka (Old Norse: [ˈkrɑːkɑ]) or Kráka, is a figure in Norse mythology. She is mentioned in the Prose Edda, the Völsunga Saga, and the Saga of Ragnar Lothbrok as one of Ragnar’s wives.

Aslaug in Legend

According to the 13th-century Saga of Ragnar Lothbrok, Aslaug was the daughter of Sigurd and the shieldmaiden Brynhildr, but she was raised by Brynhildr’s foster father, Heimir.

item.title: Bjorn Ironside
item.description:
Björn Ironside – Legendary King of the Northern Seas

Björn Ironside (Swedish: Björn Järnsida, Old Norse: Bjǫrn Járnsíða) is one of the most renowned figures in Viking Age Scandinavian legend. In the sagas and medieval chronicles, he is described as a powerful sea-king, King of Sweden, and a son of Ragnar Lothbrok.

Historical accounts of him are fragmentary and interwoven with legend, yet most scholars place his activity in the 9th century. Written sources mention him roughly between 855 and 858, when Viking fleets were actively raiding the territories of the Frankish realm.

item.title: Blenda is the heroine of a Swedish legend
item.description:
Blenda is a legendary heroine in Swedish folklore, best known from the tradition of Blendasägnen, which originates in the historical province of Småland in southern Sweden. According to the tale, she led the women of the Värend region and orchestrated a cunning attack on a Danish army that had invaded the defenseless lands.

The legend has become an important part of the region’s heritage and a symbol of female courage and resourcefulness in Scandinavian epic tradition.

item.title: Ragnar Lothbrok
item.description:
Ragnar Lothbrok

Ragnar Lothbrok (Old Norse: Ragnarr loðbrók, meaning “Ragnar Hairy-Breeches”) is a legendary Scandinavian warrior, ruler, and hero of the Viking Age. In the traditions, he appears as a powerful king associated with Denmark and Sweden, and as one of the most famous leaders of maritime expeditions in the 9th century.

The stories of Ragnar survive in Old Norse poetry, Icelandic sagas, and medieval chronicles. According to these sources, he led numerous campaigns against the British Isles and the Frankish lands, gaining renown for his boldness and military skill. In the legendary sagas, his father is named as the Swedish king Sigurd Ring.
